label: text
text: After the death of her husband, who was killed in the war, Mrs. Passenger, of 67 Rinsale Road, London, became a rescher of gymnastics to young ladies. Interviewed by a London journalist recently, Mrs. Passenger expressed no doubt as to the value of judicious gymnastics training to girls but gave it as her experience that there are times when strenuous physical exercises had best be set aside, and other means adopted to build up the system before these can be safely and profitably resumed. As instances she quoted the cases of her daughter and of a girl pupil.

label: text
text: "My daughter, Irone," said Mrs. Passenger, "was very delicate from birth. Few expected her to live, she seemed so frail. As time went on she did not improve, but grew into a feeble pale-faced child, weak and nervous. She was "anicky" with her food, and often refused things I had got specially for her. Your after year Irene went on like this, and at 16 she was anatomic, pale and nervous.

label: text
text: My husbs, d having been killed in the war, I had to find Irene soon occupation, and she obtained a position where her duties were very light, but even this proved too much for her and she had to give up her work. She grew worse than ever, her nervousness increased, and she suffered from severe headaches. I consulted a doctor, and he gave me to understand that the only thing that could save Irene was Mr. her to undergo a special operation, but I did not like the idea.

label: text
text: The Chinese police and military yesterday were compelled to fire on striking millworkers, wounding eight, mostly in the legs.

label: text
text: Many were killed and wounded and three hundred arrested to-day when Chinese guards were compelled to fire on a very large crowd on the scene of yesterday's shooting. No details are at present available.

label: text
text: The "Peking and Tientsin Times" reports that it is was believed that a settlement had been reached in the strike of the mill-workers, and the police were accordingly withdrawn. However, trouble broke out again yesterday, following the efforts of agitators from the native city, who were sent to the mills and the Russian Bund to endeavour to cause a strike among the workers of the British-American Tobacco Company.

label: text
text: Some of the millworkers were very reluctant to strike but were intimidated by strikers armed with sticks and stones. Strong police guards were sent to the mills, and were later reinforced by a hundred Fengtien soldiers.

label: text
text: All the afternoon the strikers formed processions, making threats. Shortly after six o'clock the temper of the crowds became uglier and stones were thrown at the police. Attempts were made to rush the mills, culminating in an attempt to rush the police and military cordon at the mill outside the Belgian Concession. The guards then fired, wounding eight. A Foreign eye-witness states that about two hundred shots were fired into the crowd which dispersed immediately. The situation is at present quiet.

text: “Le Journal’s” Madrid correspondent learns that landing operations at Alhucemas will begin as soon as the French offensive is launched.

label: text
text: "L'Echo de Paris," detailing the reorganisation of the Moroccan front, says that reserves in two divisions are concentrating behind the line between Fez and Taza. The whole French force is strongly equipped, notably with new, quickfiring rifles. Marshal Petain returns to Morocco to inaugurate new measures.

label: text
text: A message from Fez says that Abd el Krim is organising his defence along the entire front and preparing strong lines of trenches before Sheshuan.

label: text
text: The papers state that France and Spain cannot answer the communication made to General Primo de Rivera by the Riffman émissary. Morocco's political status was settled by international agreement and it is impossible to take up a discussion on the independence of the Riff.

label: text
text: “Le Matin” says that Abd el Krim's message can only be interpreted as voluntary ignorance of the Franco-Spanish propositions. “L'Echo de Paris” announces that Marshal Petain will soon return to Morocco to approve finally the new organization on the front.

text: The Foreign Office states that it is holding conversations with America concerning the scope of the tariff conference.

label: text
text: Japan is desirous of confining the agenda within the limits agreed at the Washington Conference but it is understood that America will consider enlarging the scope and suggesting the granting of tariff autonomy to China. The Foreign Office spokesman emphasises that Japan is unable to initiate a policy as all the Powers are suspicious of Japan's action toward China.

label: text
text: Admiral Sir Edward Seymour had some exciting and surprising reminiscences to narrate to an "Evening News" representative, when interviewed on his 85th birthday. He commenced with a tale about pirates.

label: text
text: “We were off the coast of Africa when we heard that a British ship had been captured. So off we went in search.

label: text
text: “At last we located them in their stronghold ashore, up the Congo. They were about as pretty a lot of cut-throats as you could wish to see.

label: text
text: “They outnumbered us, too, but we decided to attack.”

label: text
text: "Warm work it was while it lasted, for they were armed with rifles, but we harried them out at last, and I took one of the chiefs—a villainous-looking customer—to Ascension Island, where he served a long term of imprisonment.

label: text
text: "Most of the others escaped, but we broke up the gang (and a bullet broke my leg), and that was the main point."

label: text
text: It was in 1852, when he was only a boy of just over 12, that Sir Edward joined a sailing ship of the line at Spithead.

label: text
text: "Those were the good old days when midshipmen had to go before the mast with not too much to eat; when they had to learn their job as best they could for lack of teachers and when they had to fight their battles unaided." Ultimately Sir Edward got to his uncle's snip, the Calcutta, on active service in the China Seas.

label: text
text:
He is proud of the record of that ship, for of its midshipmen 17 became captains in the R. N. and 8 became admirals, "and I doubt whether any other ship can show that record," said Sir Edward.
